# A unit arm asserts DragCoordinator.sortZones is empty, under 4 workers

## Context

`test/playwright/unit/dashboard/CrossWindowDragTarget.spec.mjs:54` — *"an incomplete registry identity never registers (§2.3: sortGroup + windowId are mandatory)"* — reds the `unit` job intermittently, on branches that touch none of the code it exercises. Today alone it has carried a red on #18783 (a menu change), #18773 ×2 (a grid change) and #18784's branch, and a same-SHA rerun on #18773 reproduced it rather than clearing it.

The job is **right** to go red. `test/playwright/playwright.config.unit.mjs:28` sets `failOnFlakyTests: isCI` beside `retries: 2` — a flake that retries green still fails CI, which is the policy that keeps flakes from becoming background noise. Nothing here proposes changing that; the arm is what needs fixing.

Measured while shipping #18781, twelve full-suite runs on one branch and eight on `dev` source in the same worktree:

| condition | result |
|---|---|
| the spec alone, either head | 3/3 green |
| full suite, `dev` source | 0 failures in 8 runs |
| full suite, an engine branch | 3 failures in 12 runs, clustered in one window |

Not attributable to any diff. The arm is order- and load-dependent, which is exactly what asserting a shared global under parallel workers produces.

## The Problem

```js
const target = Neo.create(CrossWindowDragTarget, {windowId: 3});

expect(DragCoordinator.sortZones.size).toBe(0);
```

`DragCoordinator` is a singleton and `sortZones` is its process-global registry. `playwright.config.unit.mjs` runs `fullyParallel: true` with `workers: 4`, so each worker process runs many spec files in one shared module registry — and the arm's claim is not about the component it just created, it is about **everything in that process**. Any spec sharing the worker that registers a sort zone and has not yet destroyed it makes the assertion false, without either spec being wrong.

The intent is narrow and correct: a target created without `sortGroup` must not register. The assertion is global, and that is the whole defect.

## The Architectural Reality

The same file already shows the shape that survives parallelism, one arm earlier:

| site | claim | parallel-safe |
|---|---|---|
| `CrossWindowDragTarget.spec.mjs:31` | `sortZones.has('dock-main')` is false after destroy | yes — names the group this arm created |
| `manager/DragCoordinator.spec.mjs:154`, `:236` | `sortZones.has('dock')` is false | yes — same shape |
| `CrossWindowDragTarget.spec.mjs:59` | `sortZones.size` is 0 | **no** — a claim about every other spec in the worker |

One greppable rule covers it: **an arm may assert the groups it created; it may not assert that the map is empty.**

- `src/manager/DragCoordinator.mjs` — `sortZones`, the singleton registry.
- `src/dashboard/dock/window/DragTarget.mjs:411` — `destroy()` unregisters only when `sortGroup && windowId != null`, which is what the arm is really checking.

## The Fix

Assert the negative the arm means: after creating a target with `windowId` and no `sortGroup`, no group in the registry holds that target. `[...sortZones.values()].some(byWindow => [...byWindow.values()].includes(target))` is false — true regardless of what else shares the worker, and still false-able by the defect it guards (a target that registers without a `sortGroup` appears in exactly one group).

Deliberately not proposed: changing `failOnFlakyTests`, adding a `beforeEach` that clears the singleton (it would hide a real leak from a sibling spec and make the suite order-dependent in the other direction), or serialising the unit project.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC-1** — the arm asserts that no registry group holds the target it created, and makes no claim about the registry's size.
- [ ] **AC-2** — red-first: with `DragTarget#destroy`'s registration guard removed (or a `sortGroup` added to the arm's config), the rewritten arm fails. An arm that cannot fail is what the size assertion degenerated into.
- [ ] **AC-3** — a seeded sibling registration in the same worker does not fail the arm, and does fail the current one. This is the contamination the ticket exists for, so it is measured rather than argued.
- [ ] **AC-4** — the full unit suite runs clean ×5 consecutively on this branch; the pre-fix rate measured 3 in 12.
- [ ] **AC-5** — a census of `sortZones.size` / equivalent global-emptiness assertions across `test/playwright/unit` is recorded here, and any second instance is fixed with it or filed.

## Out of Scope

- `unit/list/animatePlugin.spec.mjs:551`, the other arm reddening the same job — @neo-opus-grace's `defect-note`, hers to file.
- `failOnFlakyTests` and the retry policy — deliberate, and this ticket depends on them staying that way.
- `unit/main/DomEvents.spec.mjs`'s namespace restoration — #18776, the same family from the other side (state left behind rather than state assumed absent).

## Avoided Traps

- **Clearing the singleton in a hook.** It would green the arm and hide a sibling's leak in the same motion, which is how a suite stops being able to report contamination at all.
- **Blaming the last diff that reddened.** Twelve runs against eight say it is neither; a flake that follows the branch you happen to be on is a scheduling artifact, not evidence.
- **Serialising the project.** The parallelism is the point of a 4200-arm suite finishing in 23 seconds; one arm's global claim does not get to spend that.
